[RTCT.6.7.6] **Old-reader rejection (structural, no minor
gate).** A runtime implementing this clause MUST accept both
encodings. A runtime built *before* this clause rejects a
compact contract **without needing to know about it**, via the
load-time hash recompute it already performs ([RTCT.6.5] /
[RDSC.16.3.3] step 3 / [RBND.4b]): it decodes the compact body
as a legacy body with an empty `nodes` list, recomputes the
canonical hash over that empty list, and the result cannot
equal the stored `rt_config_sha256` (computed over the *N*-node
logical contract, `N > 0`), so the contract is
`DS_ERR_CONTRACT_INVALID`. No version gate and no
field-presence sniffing are required. The `node_count = 0` case
([RTCT.6.7.2]) is the sole contract an old reader accepts —
correctly, as it hashes identically under either encoding.
(`[RTCT.3.3]`'s per-node coverage rule is **compile-time** —
`DS_VALIDATE_COMPILE_CONTRACT_INCOMPLETE` — and MUST NOT be cited
for runtime rejection.)
